solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Excellent Greek character, very loud in chorus?

indicators.note: in tells us the Greek letter and the loudness mark go inside the word for chorus

parts.note: to chorus is to sing together
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
ff (fortissimo) is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A splendid Greek actor booming out his part in the chorus of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chorus' reads as a noun on the surface but is the verb SING here.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiffing is dated British slang for splendid or first-rate.

clue.text: Piece of winter equipment son put on shelf

indicators.note: in a down entry, put on means placed above, so the son's letter comes first

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
a ledge is a shelf

explanation.surface: A boy's winter gear stored up on a shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge is a vehicle on runners used for sliding over snow.

clue.text: Godlessness of little devil, one yet needing reform

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: reform means reshape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An irreligious young rascal who still has to mend his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Impiety is lack of reverence for God, irreligion.

clue.text: Athletics competitor may be entered thus, expecting terrible punishment

definitions.text: Athletics competitor may be entered thus
definitions.meaning: a jumper is entered in the high jump event
an idiom meaning in serious trouble, about to be punished

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from the gallows: the high jump was a hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the literal event entry and the idiom for facing severe punishment fit.

clue.text: Green enthusiast turning up to protect island

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the island goes inside
turning up in a down entry means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast

explanation.surface: An environmentalist arriving to defend an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' suggests eco-campaigner but means naive; 'turning up' makes NAF, with I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Naif means naive or inexperienced, as green does.

clue.text: Cautious look in both directions

indicators.note: in both directions says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Advice for crossing a road: look carefully both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The road-safety image hides the instruction that the word itself reads identically either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A peep is a quick, furtive glance, the kind taken cautiously.

clue.text: Words of grave significance

parts.note: words inscribed on a tomb are literally significant at a grave

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' seems to mean serious, but it is the burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is an inscription on a tombstone commemorating the dead.

clue.text: Delightful prayers followed by a big chunk of Scripture

indicators.note: followed by puts the remaining pieces after the prayers

parts.note: pleas are earnest requests, prayers
NT is the New Testament, a large part of the Bible

explanation.surface: A pleasing service: prayers and then a long Bible reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant means agreeable or enjoyable, as delightful does.

clue.text: Elizabeth has upset engineers, one engineer in particular

parts.note: Bess is a pet form of Elizabeth

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Elizabeth has offended the engineers, especially one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is a British Army corps; 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Bessemer was the Victorian engineer who invented a process for making steel.

clue.text: Something growing in Japan I admire near the ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A visitor admires a plant close to the earth in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like the soil but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ginkgo, an ancient tree with fan-shaped leaves, is widely planted in Japan.

clue.text: No longer cheeky, is tyke finally showing skill?

parts.note: ex- means former, no longer
pert means impudent or cheeky
taken as written

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word tyke

explanation.surface: Has the once-cheeky little rascal finally learned some talent?
explanation.walkthrough: A tyke is a mischievous child; 'No longer cheeky' hides the pun ex-pert, a former cheeky one.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise is specialist knowledge or ability, i.e. a high level of competence.

clue.text: Animated adult wanting wickedness overthrown

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: overthrown says the word for wickedness is turned upside down, read backwards in this across entry

parts.note: evil means wickedness

explanation.surface: A lively grown-up who would like to see wickedness defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' is only a link here; 'overthrown' turns EVIL into LIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lively and full of energy is a figurative sense of animated, as in someone very much awake.

clue.text: Writer departs not having finished article

indicators.note: not having finished says the word for departs loses its last letter

parts.note: goes means departs
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An author walks off without completing his article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a piece of writing but is the grammatical article THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe was the German poet, novelist and dramatist who wrote Faust.

clue.text: Old vehicles that may be adapted for crusades

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters of crusades are rearranged

explanation.surface: Second-hand motors that could be converted for holy wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand automobiles sold on are previously owned, hence old vehicles.

clue.text: You and philosopher will entertain princess, and sister will go about greeting musician

parts.note: ye is the archaic plural form of you

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the princess sits inside the philosopher

parts.note: David Hume was a Scottish philosopher
Di is Princess Diana

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it, so the sister encloses the greeting

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A social scene: you and a thinker host a princess while a sister goes round saying hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' gives the archaic form; 'will entertain' and 'will go about' each signal a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Yehudi Menuhin was a celebrated American-born British violinist and conductor.

clue.text: Detectives turning up about nasty upset in connection with powerful family

indicators.note: about means around, so the detectives surround the jumbled letters
turning up in a down entry means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

indicators.note: upset means disturbed, so the letters of nasty are jumbled

explanation.surface: Police turn up over some nasty trouble linked to a mighty clan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' reverses the detectives to DIC, which goes 'about' the jumbled letters signalled by 'upset'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynastic describes a line of hereditary rulers, a powerful family.

clue.text: What's soft and 'ideous say when served up as prison food?

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
Cockney horrid without its h, standing in for hideous; and joins it on

indicators.note: served up in a down entry means the word goes upwards, backwards

parts.note: eg means for example, say

explanation.surface: A grumble about mushy, horrible jail grub.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is both oat gruel and British slang for a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal gruel is a stock prison meal, and doing time is slang for the same word.

clue.text: Coo at grannies, funny old folk

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters of the phrase are jumbled

explanation.surface: Cooing over grandmothers, those amusing elderly people.
explanation.definitionFit: People in their eighties are elderly, so they are old folk.

clue.text: Finding time to get to the Sport of Kings

parts.note: horse racing is traditionally called the Sport of Kings

explanation.surface: Making time to go to the horse races.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracing a lost person or item means locating it.

clue.text: Emissary is given a little money to try to get business

definitions.note: an emissary is a person dispatched on a mission

parts.note: a sen is a small Japanese coin
to tout is to solicit custom

explanation.surface: A messenger is handed some cash to go drumming up trade.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is by definition dispatched abroad on someone's behalf.

clue.text: Tiny boy, see, being early

parts.note: Tiny Tim is the boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol
Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop's see

explanation.surface: A small lad, look, arriving ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a common crossword example.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in good time, opportune, can be called early in that loose sense.

clue.text: Maybe book fair is subject to some changes

parts.note: a book, for one, is something read; read as an adjective describes it
just means fair

explanation.surface: A book fair might be undergoing a few alterations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book fair' reads as one event, but the two words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To readjust something is to alter it slightly, putting it through small changes.

clue.text: British character formerly attached to one Asian state

parts.note: a rune is a letter of an ancient alphabet, a character used formerly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A former British personality attached to an Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of an old alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small sultanate on the island of Borneo in South-East Asia.

clue.text: A single time just after church

parts.note: on means immediately after, as in on arrival
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: One occasion only, straight after the service.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means on one occasion only.

clue.text: Belief conveyed by code is mysterious

indicators.note: conveyed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A faith transmitted through a secret code.
explanation.definitionFit: Deism is a creed holding that God exists but does not intervene, a kind of belief.

clue.text: One lying down in Oxford?

parts.note: an Oxford is a style of shoe; the piece lying along its bottom, inside, is the lining under the foot

explanation.surface: Someone lying about, perhaps a lazy student, in the university city.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford suggests the university, but it is a lace-up shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The insole is the layer lying flat inside a shoe beneath the wearer's foot.

clue.text: Advantage of protection in the East End?

indicators.note: Cockney speech of London's East End drops the initial h, so the word loses that letter

parts.note: a hedge is protection, as against financial loss

explanation.surface: The benefit of having security in a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is a working-class area of London whose Cockney accent drops H sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a slight superiority over rivals, as in having the edge.

clue.text: Not long ago bank would keep a bit of money

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so the coin goes within

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: Lately a bank would keep back a small sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is not a financial institution but the verb, as in bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means lately, at a time just past.
